xBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4941: Agent MCP and bots (W-SEC1): request_secret

narratives.Problem: An agent that needs an API key or password has no safe way to get one: asking in chat puts the value into its transcript and logs. Epic PAN-4927 FR-7/NFR-2 require that an agent ask the operator through the dashboard and that the value reach only that agent, as a 0600 file, never a transcript, tool argument or log.
narratives.Proposal: An in-memory agent request store (services/agent-requests.ts, shared later with W-LINK1) backs two agent-token self routes (POST /api/self/secret-requests, GET .../:id/wait with 50 s chunks) and three operator routes (GET /api/agent-requests; root-credential-only POST .../:id/secret and .../:id/decline). Delivery writes <owner dir>/secrets/<NAME> (0600 in 0700) via temp + rename, logs an activity entry without the value, and refuses a stopped agent. Two agent-only MCP tools (request_secret, secret_wait) proxy the self routes. The Decisions panel shows each request as an AgentRequestCard with a masked input that only a root session can use. Token revocation deletes the secrets directory. An in-process integration test proves the canary value appears in the file and in no response, tool result, activity entry or console call (AC-12).
narratives.NonGoals:
- No way to answer a secret request from a phone, a linked machine's browser, a bot or any access token; answer routes accept only the internal token or the root session.
- No machine-link request kind routes, card or machineLink frontend kind (W-LINK1, PAN-4942); the store only carries the type members.
- No MCP server or instructions injection into agents (W-INJ1 PAN-4932, W-INJ4).
- No persistence of requests across a dashboard restart.
- No isolation between agents running as the same Unix user, no encryption at rest, no rotation.
- No pan CLI verb for requesting or answering secrets.
- The value must never appear in any HTTP response, MCP tool result, activity entry, console call, error message, URL, argv or env.
- No background expiry timer started at boot.

autoDecisions.summary: The store types include the machine-link kind and linked status, but only the secret kind is implemented.
autoDecisions.rationale: Epic W-SEC1 names the store as shared with W-LINK1 (PAN-4942); typing it now avoids a reshape, while implementing only secret keeps this issue minimal.

autoDecisions.summary: Expiry is lazy (checked on every store call, wait timer bounded by expiresAt) instead of a 30 s background timer.
autoDecisions.rationale: Observably identical, starts nothing at boot, and is deterministic under fake timers.

autoDecisions.summary: A repeated ask for the same name by the same agent returns the existing pending request (200, same requestId).
autoDecisions.rationale: An agent retrying after a lost reply must not stack duplicate cards for the operator.

autoDecisions.summary: Delivery to an agent whose token is revoked is refused with 409 agent-stopped and the request expires.
autoDecisions.rationale: Revocation already deleted the secrets directory; a later write would leave a secret on disk that nothing cleans up.

autoDecisions.summary: A request is its own Decision row (id = request id, kinds ['secretRequest'], blocking, agentRequest field) rendered by AgentRequestCard; phones show 'Answer on the desktop'.
autoDecisions.rationale: The generic Answer button reopens the AskUserQuestion dialog and an agent with both a question and a request would collide on the row key; the agent is parked in secret_wait, so it is blocking.

autoDecisions.summary: After a dashboard restart the wait answers 404 unknown-request (not expired) and the tool tells the agent to ask again.
autoDecisions.rationale: The store is in memory, so the id is genuinely unknown after a restart; the epic's 'expired' wording cannot be implemented without persistence.

autoDecisions.summary: AC-12 is proven on this branch by an in-process integration test with a real minted agent token and the real gate; the live transcript search runs after PAN-4932 (W-INJ1) merges, and browser UAT checks the Decisions panel loads with an empty /api/agent-requests list.
autoDecisions.rationale: No launch path mints agent tokens until W-INJ1 lands, so no live agent can call request_secret on this branch.

items.title: Add the in-memory agent request store and the secret file writer

narrative.Action: PRD .pan/drafts/PAN-4941.md WI-1. Create src/dashboard/server/services/agent-requests.ts exactly as WI-1 specifies: AgentRequestKind ('secret' | 'machine-link'), AgentRequestStatus, AgentRequestView, the limit constants (20 pending per agent, 10 min default, 1..60 min, 1 h ended TTL, name pattern ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$, 65,536-byte value cap), agentRequestOwnerDir(caller) (getAgentDir from lib/agents/agent-state-read.js; conversationStateDir from lib/overdeck/conversation-pane-role.js with fallback conv-<name>), createAgentRequests({ now, newId }) with createSecret / getForCaller / wait / listPending / getForAnswer / settle, the exported singleton agentRequests, and writeAgentSecretFile(ownerDir, name, value) (mkdir 0700 + chmod 0700, writeFile <name>.<uuid>.partial with flag wx mode 0600, rename, unlink partial on error). Expiry is lazy (D-3): every method first expires overdue pending requests and prunes ended ones; wait's timer is min(timeout, expiresAt-now) and copies the race in services/self-jobs.ts wait(). A repeated ask for the same name by the same agent returns the pending request with created:false (D-6). Use node:fs/promises only; no *Sync calls. Tests use vi.useFakeTimers and vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync.

items.title: Given one agent, when it asks twice for the same name, then createSecret returns created: false and the same 32-hex id, and the 21st distinct pending request of that agent returns code too-many-requests while another agent's ask still succeeds.
Given another agent's request id, when getForCaller or wait is called, then each returns null.
Given a pending request on fake timers, when settle runs during a wait the wait resolves at once with the new status, and when expiresAt passes first the wait resolves with status expired.

Given writeAgentSecretFile, when it delivers a value, then it creates <ownerDir>/secrets/<name> with mode 0600 in a directory with mode 0700, tightens an existing 0755 secrets directory to 0700, leaves no .partial file, and rejects the name ../X.
Add POST /api/self/secret-requests and its 50 s wait route

narrative.Action: PRD WI-2. New top-level route file routes/self-requests.ts with pure handlers handleSecretRequestCreate(credential, bodyText, deps) and handleSecretRequestWait(credential, id, rawTimeout, signal, deps), and makeSelfRequestsRouteLayer / selfRequestsRouteLayer, shaped like routes/self-jobs.ts. Caller via selfCallerFromCredential; body parsed with a swallowing parseJsonObject copied from routes/pairing.ts (never let JSON.parse errors escape); validation codes bad-body, bad-name, bad-prompt, bad-timeout (timeoutMs 60000..3600000); 201 created / 200 existing (D-6) / 429 too-many-requests; success body { requestId, status: 'pending', expiresAt, next: { tool: 'secret_wait', arguments: { requestId } } }. Wait reuses parseWaitTimeoutMs exported from routes/self-jobs.ts; unknown or foreign id answers 404 { code: 'unknown-request' } with the restart hint; delivered answers { requestId, status, file }; never a value. No CSRF helper on self routes (D-5). Add the two route-scope rows (POST tell, GET wait read:state) after the W-SELF1 rows, the two no-loss rows after the W-SELF1 rows, and register selfRequestsRouteLayer in server.ts next to selfJobsRouteLayer. Tests go in a WI-2 describe block of agent-requests-routes.test.ts using the temp OVERDECK_HOME + real gate setup from self-jobs-routes.test.ts.

items.title: Given an agent token, when it posts a valid { name, prompt }, then the route returns 201 with next.tool equal to secret_wait, and posting the same ask again returns 200 with the same requestId.
Given a root-session credential, when it posts to /api/self/secret-requests, then the route returns 403 with code not-an-agent-token.

Given bad input (name 'bad', empty prompt, timeoutMs 5, a non-JSON body), when posted by an agent token, then the route returns 400 with codes bad-name, bad-prompt, bad-timeout and bad-body respectively.
Given a pending request on fake timers, when its owner waits, then the wait returns status pending with next after 50 s, and another agent's wait on the same id returns 404 with code unknown-request.
Given the real remote request gate, when a token holding only read:state posts to /api/self/secret-requests, then the gate rejects it with 403 insufficient_scope.
Add root-only answer and decline routes plus the pending list route

narrative.Action: PRD WI-3. New top-level route file routes/agent-requests.ts: GET /api/agent-requests (rows without value, result or owner directory), POST /api/agent-requests/:id/secret and POST /api/agent-requests/:id/decline. Both POSTs call rejectUnsafeDashboardMutationRequest first, then require credential kind internal-token or root-session (403 code root-only), and answer with Cache-Control no-store. Secret handler order: root check, swallowing body parse with fixed 400 bad-value text (never echo the body), getForAnswer (404 unknown-request, 409 wrong-kind, 409 not-pending with status), D-7 active-agent-token check via listAccessTokens (409 agent-stopped and settle expired, no write), writeAgentSecretFile in try/catch logging error.name only (500 write-failed), settle delivered, emitActivityEntry 'Secret <name> delivered to <label>', 200 { requestId, status: 'delivered' }. Decline: root check, 404/409, settle declined, activity 'Secret <name> declined for <label>'. Add the GET read:conversations scope row plus a comment that the two POSTs have no row on purpose (D-4); three no-loss rows; register agentRequestsRouteLayer in server.ts. Tests go in a WI-3 describe block of agent-requests-routes.test.ts.

items.title: Given the real remote request gate, when a token holding approve (or a device) posts to /api/agent-requests/:id/secret or /decline, then it is rejected with 403, and calling the handler directly with a non-root credential returns 403 with code root-only.

Given a pending secret request, when a root session posts { value }, then the route returns 200 status delivered, the file is created with mode 0600 in a 0700 directory, and a second answer returns 409 not-pending.
Given a request whose agent token has been revoked, when a root session posts a value, then the route returns 409 agent-stopped, no file is written, and the owner's wait returns status expired.
Given a malformed body that contains a canary string, when posted to the secret route, then the route returns 400 bad-value and neither the response nor any console.* spy call contains the canary.
Given pending requests, when GET /api/agent-requests is called with read:conversations, then it returns rows with id, name, prompt and label and no value, result or owner-directory field.
Delete the secrets directory when an agent's tokens are revoked

narrative.Action: PRD WI-4. In revokeAgentMcpTokens (src/lib/mcp/agent-token.ts), inside the existing `if (dir !== undefined)` block after the mcp-token unlink, add `await rm(join(dir, 'secrets'), { recursive: true, force: true });` (import rm from node:fs/promises) and update the doc comment. It stays inside the existing try, so it never throws.

items.title: Given an agent owner directory holding secrets/KEY, when revokeAgentMcpTokens(agentId) runs, then the secrets directory no longer exists.
Given a conversation revoke with { agentKind: 'conversation', dir }, when it runs, then <dir>/secrets is deleted.
Given no secrets directory, when revokeAgentMcpTokens runs, then it resolves with the revoked count and logs no warning.
Add the request_secret and secret_wait agent tools

expected_outputs: every test file under tests/unit/lib/mcp/ passes

narrative.Action: PRD WI-5. Add request_secret (scope tell, audience agent, POST /api/self/secret-requests with { name, prompt, timeoutMs? }) and secret_wait (scope read:state, audience agent, GET /api/self/secret-requests/<encoded id>/wait?timeoutMs=50000) to tools-self.ts with the verbatim descriptions in the PRD; SELF_TOOLS = [waitJob, requestSecret, secretWait]; both return routeResult(response). Update the pinned tests: tools-approve.test.ts ALL_TOOLS order appends request_secret, secret_wait; visibility.test.ts read:state agent list becomes ['list_machines', 'wait_job', 'secret_wait']; tool-annotations.test.ts SINGLE_ROUTE_PATHS gains both tools' routes; tools-self.test.ts covers both tools.

items.title: Given a non-agent token, when tools/list runs, then neither request_secret nor secret_wait is listed and calling either returns Unknown tool.
Given an agent token with only read:state, when tools/list runs, then it lists list_machines, wait_job and secret_wait and not request_secret.
Given request_secret with name and prompt, when called, then it posts exactly { name, prompt } to /api/self/secret-requests, and a call without name returns a tool error before any request.
Given secret_wait with requestId a/b, when called, then it requests /api/self/secret-requests/a%2Fb/wait?timeoutMs=50000, and a 404 route answer becomes a tool error starting HTTP 404.
Prove AC-12: the value reaches a 0600 file and no output

expected_outputs: the 'secret request flow (AC-12)' describe block passes

narrative.Action: PRD WI-6. Add a final describe('secret request flow (AC-12)') block to agent-requests-routes.test.ts: under the temp OVERDECK_HOME, mint a real agent token with createAccessToken({ kind: 'token', agentId: 'agent-pan-1', agentKind: 'agent', role: 'work', scopes: [...] }), spy on console.log/info/warn/error/debug, vi.mock activity-logger to capture emitActivityEntry args, build an MCP client with createOverdeckMcpServer({ api, scopes, isAgent: true }) whose api.request dispatches into the route handlers with the agent credential, then run request_secret → GET /api/agent-requests (root session) → POST secret with a random canary (root session) → secret_wait.

items.title: Given the full flow with a random canary, when the root session delivers it, then <home>/agents/agent-pan-1/secrets/<NAME> contains exactly the canary with mode 0600 in a 0700 directory.
Given the same flow, when every route answer, MCP tool result, captured emitActivityEntry argument and console.* spy call is JSON-stringified, then the canary appears zero times.
Given the same flow, when delivery completes, then exactly one activity entry reads 'Secret <NAME> delivered to agent-pan-1 · PAN-1' and secret_wait returns status delivered with the file path.
